A.explanation: 2 would count only one down quark per neutron and miss the down quark in the proton.

B.explanation: 3 is the total number of nucleons in $^{3}_{1}	ext{H}$, not the total number of down quarks.

C.explanation: 4 would count the two neutrons correctly but miss the one down quark in the single proton.

D.explanation: 1 proton gives 1 down quark and 2 neutrons give 4 down quarks, for a total of 5 down quarks.

hints: Notice the notation $^{3}_{1}	ext{H}$ gives proton number 1 and nucleon number 3, so work out how many protons and neutrons are in the nucleus.
Recall the quark make-up: proton is $uud$ and neutron is $udd$, so count how many down quarks each nucleon contributes.
Add the down quarks from 1 proton to the down quarks from 2 neutrons to get the total for the nucleus.
walkthrough: Read $^{3}_{1}	ext{H}$: lower number 1 is proton number $Z$, upper number 3 is nucleon number $A$.
So number of protons $= 1$ and number of neutrons $= A - Z = 3 - 1 = 2$.
Use the quark model: a proton is $uud$ so it contains 1 down quark, and a neutron is $udd$ so it contains 2 down quarks.
